public_rationale: The evidence shows both delivered capacity and an example of expensive borrowing. That makes a literal claim of zero construction untenable, but the ordinary broader reading concerns stalled delivery and dependence across the industry. Individual projects and a general data-center spending series do not settle that claim. The record is insufficient to label the whole statement supported, contradicted, or mixed.
limitations: A literal zero-construction interpretation would produce a different assessment.
Construction spending is not commissioned capacity.
A high coupon on one project's debt does not establish widespread financing dependence.

statement.excerpt: Data centers are not getting built, and are requiring endless high-interest debt to fund them.

from_speaker: Data centers are not getting built
requiring endless high-interest debt to fund them
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion identifies AI data centers as the subject.

Use July through September 2026, the latest completed quarter before the post, for this ongoing construction and financing observation. Evidence may cover a subperiod within that quarter without establishing the whole quarter.
Read not getting built as a broad failure to progress or deliver the planned buildout, rather than literally no construction anywhere.
Read endless as repeated dependence on borrowing, not an infinite quantity.
High-interest requires comparison with contemporaneous financing of comparable risk, maturity, and security. One expensive bond cannot establish sector-wide dependence.
criteria.support_condition: Representative construction and completion records show a broad stall relative to the planned AI buildout, while representative financing records establish dependence on repeated borrowing at materially expensive comparable terms.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative physical construction or completion records show substantial continued progress, or representative financing records show the buildout is not broadly dependent on repeated expensive debt.
